findings.summary: OR-10 mandates a repository-bound corpus of exactly 20 `sanitized-real` originator prompts, but `sanitized-real` is only a classification label: the Exam defines no prohibited-field or re-identification oracle, source-to-fixture sanitization test, provenance or use-authorization record, or raw-source disposition. A8 inventories the stored fixture, while the accepted retention policy has no record-class schedule or canonical lifecycle trigger for a sanitized-real evaluation corpus or its derived versions. The corpus can therefore satisfy OR-10 and every stated crawl while retaining originator content or identifiers indefinitely in Git, history, forks, caches, and backups without a deterministic privacy verdict.
findings.requiredResolution: Make `sanitized-real` a revision-bound, testable privacy class: define prohibited direct and quasi-identifiers, re-identification and free-text leakage criteria, source provenance and authorized-use evidence, an independently reproducible source-to-fixture sanitization/inspection procedure, and fail-closed results for every prompt and derived form. Assign the corpus, predecessors, generated baselines, failure shrinks, histories, forks, caches, and backup copies to exact retention-policy classes with canonical triggers, expiry/hold/deletion outcomes, and verified raw-source disposition; preserve the separate production-versus-fixture credentials and destinations.

escalations.reason: PRIV-G2-R2-001 is an unresolved major Exam-adequacy finding for a mandatory real-originator evaluation corpus.
The Exam provides no deterministic sanitization, provenance, authorized-use, raw-source-disposition, or retention-class evidence contract for the required sanitized-real prompt corpus.
Committing real-originator prompt derivatives to Git and propagated provider copies without a complete sanitization and lifecycle oracle can materially affect originator privacy rights.
